target.title: Supplier approval records
target.frame: A nonprofit requires documented approval before staff place supplier orders above an internal spending threshold. A quarterly review found that 14 of 90 sampled orders lack an approval attachment in the purchasing system. Approvals may also be recorded in meeting minutes or delegated-authority forms. The operations lead must prepare a defensible account of what happened and decide which records or process changes to pursue before the board review in three weeks. The internal rule is given; no legal conclusion is requested.

instrument.state: An object's history is only partially known, but dispersed records may preserve dated traces of ownership, custody, transfer, location, or transaction.
instrument.operation: Gather and cross-check records that can link the object to successive people, places, and transactions, arranging supported links into a chronology and marking unsupported intervals as gaps.
instrument.signal: Independent records form compatible chronological links between successive states of ownership or custody, while contradictions and missing intervals expose uncertainty in the reconstructed sequence.
instrument.inference: The compatible links support a bounded reconstruction of the object's documented history, including which transitions are established and where provenance remains unresolved.
instrument.limit: Records may be lost, inaccessible, anonymous, forged, mistaken, or copied from one another; names and descriptions may be ambiguous; absence of a record does not establish absence of a transfer; and a continuous-looking chronology can still contain undocumented or misidentified transitions.

mapping.state: Treat each of the 14 sampled orders lacking a purchasing-system approval attachment as a transaction with a partially documented history. The supplied finding establishes an attachment gap, not that approval was absent. For each order, establish its identity, value, placement date, applicable threshold and approval requirements, and the authority of any purported approver. Do not assume all 14 required approval or that meeting minutes or delegated-authority forms necessarily satisfy the rule.
mapping.operation: Preserve the original review finding and gather each flagged order's purchasing record, dated approval records, relevant meeting minutes, delegated-authority forms and available audit history. Cross-check order identifiers, supplier, amount, scope, people and dates across these sources. Reconstruct the supported sequence from any delegation of authority through approval to order placement and later attachment or amendment. Distinguish the date approval reportedly occurred from the date its documentation was created or uploaded; a delegation establishes authority only within its terms and does not by itself establish approval of a particular order. Identify copied or derivative records rather than counting them as independent corroboration. Mark unsupported intervals and conflicting links explicitly. Request missing originals or clarification from relevant record custodians, recording searches, responses and remaining uncertainty. Set a reporting cutoff before the board review in three weeks. Close a case when applicability and the relevant sequence are adequately supported; otherwise stop active reconstruction at the cutoff, or when identified sources are exhausted or inaccessible, and report the case as unresolved with a named follow-up owner and next step. Link recovered records to their orders while retaining their actual dates and the original attachment-gap finding.
mapping.signal: Look for independently originating records that agree on the same order, an approver's authority at the relevant time, the scope of approval and its documented occurrence before placement. Observe separately whether an attachment was merely uploaded later, whether documentation was first created after placement, or whether approval itself occurred afterward. Conflicting dates, mismatched amounts or identities, unclear delegation terms, unsupported retrospective statements and missing links signal uncertainty. Record these as proposed checks and possible findings, not as observations already made.
mapping.inference: Compatible links can support a bounded account that a particular order had documented approval before placement despite its missing attachment, provided the evidence satisfies the internal rule. Supported timing showing approval only after placement can establish that the identified approval was late, while leaving open whether another earlier approval existed. A verified exemption can establish that approval was not required for that order. Unsuccessful searches warrant saying that qualifying prior approval was not located within the recorded search scope. Prepare the board account with case-level evidence, established transitions, contradictions and unresolved gaps. Pursue attachment or indexing changes where evidence supports a filing problem; pursue authority clarification where delegation is unclear; and propose a pre-order approval check where the reconstructed sequence supports a timing or control problem. Assign unresolved record requests and any proposed changes owners and dates.
mapping.limit: Records may be missing, inaccessible, inaccurate, altered, ambiguous or copied from a common source. A later account of an earlier approval does not automatically establish contemporaneous documentation, and an upload timestamp alone does not date the approval. A complete-looking chronology may join different orders or conceal undocumented transitions. Missing attachments or unsuccessful searches do not prove that approval never occurred. Conversely, an attachment alone does not establish valid, timely approval. Do not extrapolate the 14-of-90 attachment finding into an organization-wide approval-failure rate without evidence about sampling and the remaining records. The reporting cutoff limits the investigation, not the underlying uncertainty; later evidence should trigger a dated revision. Apply the internal rule without drawing legal conclusions.

component.value: Unsuccessful searches support reporting that qualifying prior approval was not located within the recorded search scope.
component.scope: A search-bounded non-location conclusion, conditional on unsuccessful searches; it is not an assertion of approval nonexistence.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly limits the reportable conclusion to qualifying prior approval within the recorded scope.
